response.final_analysis: Aldosterone primarily acts at the collecting duct of the kidney, where it binds to mineralocorticoid receptors to increase sodium reabsorption and potassium excretion. This is a well-established fact in renal physiology, supported by extensive research and consensus in the medical community.
